paragraphs.text: # Best Summer Holiday & Vacation Destinations — What to Wear & What to Pack

Picking a summer destination is only half the challenge — knowing what to actually wear once you get there makes the difference between a trip full of great photos and one where you're either sweating through the wrong outfit or scrambling to buy something once you land. This guide covers seven of the best summer destinations for UK and US travelers, with real packing and outfit guidance for each — plus a few pieces we'd genuinely pack ourselves.
## 1. Greece
Greece remains one of the most photographed destinations in the world for good reason — whitewashed buildings, blue domes, and some of the clearest water in the Mediterranean.
**Getting there:** Direct flights from most UK airports run around 3.5–4 hours in peak season; from the US, most routes connect through a European hub.
**Where to stay:** Santorini's caldera-view hotels book out fast in summer — reserve months ahead. Athens offers more budget flexibility as a base, with easy ferry connections to the islands.
**What to do:** Sunset in Oia, the Acropolis and ancient sites in Athens, beach clubs in Mykonos.
### What to Wear in Greece
- Lightweight, breathable t-shirts — white and neutral tones photograph best against the blue-and-white backdrop
- Loose linen shirts or oversized tees for shade during the hottest hours
- Comfortable sandals for cobbled streets and boat trips
- Sunglasses and a wide-brim hat
**Our Pick:** A relaxed-fit white or sand-colored graphic tee works across every part of a Greek island trip — beach by day, taverna dinner by night. [Shop Greek Summer Tees →]
## 2. Spain
Spain covers an enormous range in one country — Barcelona's architecture, Ibiza's beach clubs, and the Costa del Sol's coastal towns.
**Getting there:** Around 2 hours direct from the UK; roughly 8–9 hours from the US East Coast.
**Where to stay:** Barcelona has strong options at every budget; Ibiza splits between lively San Antonio and quieter Santa Eulalia.
**What to do:** Gaudí's Sagrada Família and Park Güell in Barcelona, beach clubs in Ibiza, whitewashed pueblos along the Costa del Sol.
### What to Wear in Spain
- Breathable cotton tees for daytime sightseeing
- A slightly smarter tee or shirt for evening tapas and dinner
- Comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter's uneven streets
- Swimwear and a light cover-up for coastal days
**Our Pick:** A minimalist Barcelona skyline or Gaudí mosaic-print tee doubles as a souvenir you'll actually wear again. [Shop Barcelona Tees →]
## 3. Italy
From Rome's ancient ruins to the Amalfi Coast's cliffside towns, Italy delivers history and coastline in equal measure.
**Getting there:** Around 2.5–3 hours direct from the UK; 9–10 hours from the US.
**Where to stay:** Rome has options across every budget; Amalfi Coast towns like Positano get expensive fast in peak season, so book 3–4 months ahead.
**What to do:** The Colosseum and Roman Forum, coastal drives along the Amalfi Coast, beaches and ruins in Sicily.
### What to Wear in Italy
- Simple, well-fitted tees — Italian style leans understated rather than flashy
- Comfortable shoes built for cobblestones
- A light scarf or layer for cooler evenings
- Swimwear for coastal stops
**Our Pick:** A clean, retro-style Italy tee in a muted palette fits the country's understated fashion sense. [Shop Italy Travel Tees →]
## 4. Portugal
One of Western Europe's best-value destinations, with Lisbon's hills, Porto's wine cellars, and the Algarve's beaches all within easy reach.
**Getting there:** Around 2.5 hours direct from the UK; the Algarve has its own airport (Faro) for direct beach trips.
**Where to stay:** Lisbon and Porto offer strong mid-range hotels; the Algarve leans toward resort-style beachfront stays.
**What to do:** Historic trams and viewpoints in Lisbon, port wine tasting in Porto, beach-hopping along the Algarve.
### What to Wear in Portugal
- Casual, relaxed pieces — Portugal's dress code stays laid-back even at nicer restaurants
- Sun protection: hat and sunscreen, especially in the Algarve
- Comfortable shoes for Lisbon's steep streets
- A light jacket for breezy coastal evenings
**Our Pick:** An easy oversized graphic tee suits Portugal's relaxed pace better than anything structured. [Shop Portugal Tees →]
## 5. Florida, USA
A major hub for both domestic US and international travel, with beaches, theme parks, and island-hopping all on offer.
**Getting there:** Direct routes from most UK airports (9–10 hours) and virtually every major US city.
**Where to stay:** Miami ranges from budget to ultra-luxury; Orlando centers around family resort packages; the Keys favor smaller boutique stays.
**What to do:** Beaches and nightlife in Miami, theme parks in Orlando, diving and island-hopping in the Keys.
### What to Wear in Florida
- Lightweight, quick-dry fabrics — Florida's humidity is intense
- Oversized graphic tees and shorts as a practical daytime uniform
- Serious sun protection
- Swimwear for near-daily beach or pool time
**Our Pick:** A bold, oversized graphic tee handles Florida's heat and its laid-back beach-city energy equally well. [Shop Florida & Beach Tees →]
## 6. Mexico
Beach resorts, cenotes, and one of the world's great food cities, all in one country.
**Getting there:** 2–4 hours direct from major US cities; seasonal direct UK routes to Cancun run around 10–11 hours.
**Where to stay:** Cancun and Tulum range from all-inclusive resorts to boutique eco-stays; Mexico City offers strong value throughout.
**What to do:** All-inclusive beach days in Cancun, cenotes and boho beach culture in Tulum, museums and food in Mexico City.
### What to Wear in Mexico
- Relaxed beachwear for Cancun and Tulum
- Reef-safe sunscreen and light layers
- Slightly smarter casual pieces for Mexico City's restaurant scene
- A rash guard or cover-up for cenote and reef visits
**Our Pick:** A tropical-print or retro travel tee fits Mexico's beach-forward, laid-back style. [Shop Beach & Retro Travel Tees →]
## 7. The Caribbean
Classic beach-resort territory, with Jamaica, Barbados, and the Bahamas all offering their own take on island life.
**Getting there:** 3–5 hours direct from the US East Coast; around 9–10 hours direct from the UK.
**Where to stay:** All-inclusive resorts dominate, though boutique and villa options are growing for travelers wanting something less resort-heavy.
**What to do:** Beach and reef days across the islands, rum distillery tours, sailing and snorkeling in the Bahamas.
### What to Wear in the Caribbean
- Bright colors and tropical prints — this is the one destination where bold beachwear genuinely fits the vibe
- A rash guard for snorkeling
- Light cover-ups and a dressier outfit for resort dinner nights
- Comfortable sandals that can handle sand and boat decks
**Our Pick:** A bright tropical graphic tee is practically part of the Caribbean uniform. [Shop Tropical & Vacation Tees →]
## Packing Principles That Apply Everywhere
A few rules hold true no matter which destination on this list you choose:
- **Pack more t-shirts than you think you'll need** — heat and humidity mean daily changes on most summer trips
- **Mix neutral basics with one or two statement pieces** — practical for repeat wear, but still photo-ready
- **Choose breathable fabrics** — cotton or lightweight blends over anything heavy or synthetic
- **Let the destination set the tone** — minimal whites for Greece, bold tropical prints for the Caribbean, retro graphics for a road trip
